Find the area bounded between the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{4x-8},$ the $y$-axis and the lines $y=-1$ and $y=2,$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{4x-8} \\ {y}^{3} & =4x-8 \\ {y}^{3}+8 & =4x \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}{y}^{3}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}(\frac{1}{4}{y}^{3}+2)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y+2{\int }_{-1}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{-1}^{2}+2\cdot y{|}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}(16-1)+2(2+1) \\  & =\frac{15}{16}+6 \\  & =\frac{111}{16}\end{aligned}
$$
